summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with chronic pancreatitis was admitted with worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had recently been in a motor vehicle collision and had residual seatbelt-related abdominal discomfort. Imaging revealed a partial small-bowel obstruction likely due to adhesions from a prior C-section, with no evidence of acute pancreatitis. She was managed conservatively with bowel rest, IV fluids, pain control, and antiemetics. Her symptoms improved with passage of gas, bowel movements, and successful advancement to a full diet. She also reported new-onset headaches, which were managed with continuation of home medications. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with her primary care provider and gastroenterologist.
